mechanism_narrative: The collapse in TRANSIT stations to -73.6 percent below baseline reflects a broad suppression of obligatory and discretionary out-of-home trips; while transit remains below -60, retail-and-recreation footfall cannot recover, so the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC stays below its last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -41.3 to -73.6 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds -40.7 (the last-28-day mean) while TRANSIT weekly means remain below -60 throughout the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Once RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 percent above baseline, households have settled into a full home-confinement routine in which discretionary shopping trips are dropped; this keeps RETAIL_REC depressed, so the next 28-day mean sits below the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean exceeds +20.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 10.3 to 24.3 while RETAIL_REC fell from -22.7 to -50.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean within two weeks in the majority of periods where RESIDENTIAL weekly means stay above +20.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES collapsing together removes both the commuting flow and the trip-chaining on which retail-and-recreation visits depend; with both series jointly deep below baseline the compound effect drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks than over the past four.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both below -50 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT -73.6 and WORKPLACES -56.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are jointly below -50, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days is higher than the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The swing in GROCERY_PHARM from +8.0 to -22.1 shows the pantry-stocking phase is over and no compensating essential-trip frequency remains; under enforced non-essential closure this leaves RETAIL_REC on a flat-to-lower path, so the next 28-day mean is below the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses below 0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from +8.0 to -22.1 over three weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or above its last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains below 0 percent change.

mechanism_narrative: The partial rebound in PARKS from -53.1 to -42.6 while retail keeps falling indicates substitution of out-of-home activity toward open-air space and away from indoor retail; this substitution depresses RETAIL_REC over the next seven days.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean improves by more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 10.5 points from -53.1 to -42.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS improves by more than 8 points week-on-week, the following weekly RETAIL_REC mean rises rather than falls.

mechanism_narrative: High RESIDENTIAL combined with falling GROCERY_PHARM means households are drawing down stored goods and cutting overall shopping-trip frequency; this joint condition removes trips that would otherwise touch retail-and-recreation venues, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +18 and GROCERY_PHARM below -15 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:latest week shows RESIDENTIAL +24.3 and GROCERY_PHARM -22.1
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL exceeds +18 and GROCERY_PHARM is below -15, mean RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks is higher than the preceding two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Because the last 28-day RETAIL_REC mean of about -40.7 is far above the latest weekly level of -50.1, a flat continuation at the current level mechanically produces a lower next-28-day mean; the shrinking week-on-week declines (-21.4, -2.0, -4.0) reflect exhaustion of declines, not the start of a recovery.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or above -40.7 despite the latest weekly mean remaining at or below -45.

mechanism_narrative: Conditional on a formal de-escalation allowing non-essential reopening within three weeks, recovering TRANSIT and WORKPLACES lift retail footfall fast enough that the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the last 28-day mean of roughly -40.7.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 10 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: After a de-escalation announcement, TRANSIT improves more than 10 points week-on-week twice, yet mean RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days remains below -40.7.
